cross_source_ordering.observed: forkAndSpecialize invokes nativeForkAndSpecialize, then postForkCommon, then returns to ZygoteConnection.
postForkCommon invokes nativePostZygoteFork and then Daemons.startPostZygoteFork; postForkChild native initialization occurs earlier.
The existing NNP and range-filter installation occurs later in child Java initialization. It cannot retroactively constrain an earlier native-bridge initialization.

findings.implication: The first supported role must explicitly select the Java app-zygote path; this observation does not prove native-service or WebView role support, nor the upstream allocation provenance of every constructor argument.
findings.observed: The object stores the zygote UID and permitted UID/GID interval separately. The Java zygote path passes the interval to startChildZygote and waits for its socket before application preload. Native-service zygotes select a separate process interface.

findings.implication: The matched request already transports the interval, but the current native fork signature does not consume it. A new typed field must be parsed before fork, with duplicate, range, class, invocation-wrapper and requester checks.
findings.observed: startChildZygote sends --start-child-zygote and places uid-range-start/end in the extra arguments after the class name. The UID and GID of the zygote are independent outer arguments.

findings.implication: Treating mStartChildZygote alone as a provenance grant would not attest a constrained interval. The pending factory challenge must not grant creation until an actual privileged parent approves the exact interval and live child.
findings.observed: The parser stores the start-child-zygote boolean. Its final validation only establishes presence of a child socket argument; the UID interval remains in mRemainingArgs.

findings.implication: handleParentProc is not an early pre-specialization approval hook. A matched native fork handshake must complete before guest-capable child initialization and before the parent returns to the Java post-fork daemon restart.
findings.observed: mStartChildZygote selects the Java fork path. It calls Zygote.forkAndSpecialize before either handleChildProc or handleParentProc. The child later invokes childZygoteInit.

findings.implication: A persistent clone worker absent from Bionic registration can survive the last normal thread. NativeBridge fork callbacks alone do not close this host-native exit boundary. Any future hook must account for destructors/creation synchronization and both final exit paths; this review does not invent a safe hook or mark it solved.
findings.observed: Cleanup/TLS destructors precede terminating=true under the creation lock, signal blocking, dynamic TLS cleanup and thread-exit callbacks. The terminal paths invoke stack teardown or __exit(0); this function contains no raw-metadata-owner retirement or last-nonowner-thread test.

planned_implementation_not_claimed_compl.factory_authority: Separate protocol: pending kernel-PIDFD-bound child challenge; one approval from the actual live privileged parent for the same child/range/pair; per-message kernel PIDFD identity; no role-label, seccomp-count or credential-text self-attestation.
planned_implementation_not_claimed_compl.raw_worker: Zero-cap worker remains required; ordinary zero-cap provenance and NOFILE contracts stay intact. Capable-role factory authorization does not permit inherited privileged worker state.
planned_implementation_not_claimed_compl.supported_initial_role: Matched LP64 x86_64 Java AppZygoteInit path only, with trusted request parsing, early native query-only base filter and range policy installed before guest initialization. Ordinary three base-filter entrypoints remain unchanged.
unclosed: Trusted early Java/JNI range handoff and parent challenge channel have not been implemented or tested in the platform.
Actual range-policy permanence/architecture closure, credential and namespace transition behavior and paired binaries remain unqualified.
Host-native last-thread exit still needs a concrete lifetime mechanism.
Factory role registry is new local draft code; no server/client integration or actual kernel authorization positive has run.
